HRA Analysis: TOMMY MACH (5) ran on well when clear over the concluding stages last start has sound claims. PARADIGM (4) form is sound in similar grade and should be handy. STAR OF WILLOUGHBY (6) recent form sees him with a genuine chance to make it 2 wins from last 3 starts. NIGHT SPIRIT (7) is having first start for the Pullicino stable and is drawn to get a cheap run.

JILLIBY BLISS (7) racing very consistent since joining the Girardi stable and looks the one to beat. EAGLESTONE (2) is working up to a win and won’t be far away. ALDEBARAN BREE (5) improving with racing and has place claims. MAGICAL MADGE (4) looks the best of the rest on exposed form however keep a watch on markets for first starter REHAB LAD and newcomer to the Weidenbach stable EMILY MEAGAN.

This looks a drop in class for CAPTAIN PAPRIKA (5). MEET ME AT THE BEAH NZ (6) continues to race consistently and has claims despite the wide draw. MY ULTIMATE HENRY (7) should get a good trip behind GIANT JACKSON and expect be thereabouts at the finish. LOCHINVAR RULER (2) should be prominent over the short trip.

THE GOLDEN HOOK(4) was a strong effort to win last start, looks well placed and will be hard to beat here. KEAYANG MEMORY (8) solid form and looks one of the main chances. ALWAYS ON SAFARI (7) has place claims from a tricky draw. If OAKLANDER (1) can make use of the good draw it should run a forward race.

QUARTARARO (10) talented trotter when it does everything right. TINEY (8) racing well and has solid eachway claims. NOTHING I WANT (2) resumes here and expect a forward showing. PARLEZVOUS PATTY (9) will need some luck from the draw but has claims.

MACHFREDDY (1) sound effort when resuming for the Ryan stable, drawn to be prominent and should go close. LUNADIVA (6) has claims despite the wide draw. NOHASHTAGREQUIRED (5) first starter from the Bain stable may pay to keep safe. SIENNA BELLA (9) racing well however is awkwardly drawn here.

FE FE ON FIRE (5) strong effort when second at first run for the Hryhorec stable and has solid claims to go one better here. HASTY BID (2) racing well and from the draw has appeal. ALORA (3) resuming from spell and if near its best form has eachway claims. ZANY GIRL (7) awkwardly drawn with place claims.

SWEETKINDOFMAGIC (10) form before spell looked good for a race like this, awkward draw but should be hard to beat. NO GOOD REASON (1) drawn to be prominent for a long way. LAZIEST (6) will find this easier than recent runs, has solid claims. MURRA LANE (3) and IMA TIGGY TIGER are place chances. LISTEN TO THE HAND would be hard to beat if it gains a start.

A tricky race with many chances. TAKE MY WALLET NZ (2) not far away last start and drawn well here. JACKIE DANIELS (4) having first start for Hryhorec stable hasn’t won for nearly 2 years but has been racing in stronger Gloucester Park company, keep safe. RESURRECTS (9) has changed stables now in the HILL team, watch for betting moves. BALLADORO (10) awkwardly drawn and not had a lot of luck recently, place claims. OVERVIEW:KYVALLEY REEVA (3) hadn’t done much of note prior to last start, but her performance in winning her maiden was hard to ignore. John Caldow jumped aboard, pushed her forward to lead and she continued to extend, putting a gap on the opposition and winning with something in hand in solid closing sectionals. She had been unruly prior to that, so proceed with caution, but a repeat will see her hard to beat. THE PASO DOBLE (6) broke through for a terrific and deserved maiden victory last time out, showing his customary early gate speed and putting a space on his rivals. Even though he’s drawn wide, his gate manners can negate that, allowing him to look for a forward position and take running down again. RIPPING RONALDO (4) creates interest first-up from a break considering he went out on a high with a solid win at Maryborough in July. No trial into this, but this is an astute stable, so monitor betting. WHISKEY DAWN (7) will appreciate this level compared to her last two starts in stronger company, where she wasn’t too far off the winners. She’s yet to place since her maiden victory at this track, but is going okay. The draw just means she will have to work at some stage. JINXED (2) is a 3yo filly having her second start and showed good speed for a sound fourth on debut last week. She can run well again based on that performance. BACK: KYVALLEY REEVA (3)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:KYVALLEY REEVA (3), THE PASO DOBLE (6), RIPPING RONALDO (4), WHISKEY DAWN (7)

OVERVIEW:WAR ZONE (10) was held up at a vital stage last week and may have gone close to winning had he seen daylight a little earlier, and they ran decent time for this grade. He was a winner three starts back, again in good time, when able to lead. Although the draw and map do him no favours, he can sweep home with the right tempo. JUSTLIKEDAVE (7) is a horse who never seems to have much luck with barrier draws and, as a result, is often turning in nice runs from difficult positions. He gets no favours again, but this doesn’t look as strong as what he’s been opposed to. TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6) loomed up and was disappointing in the straight last time, and that was coming off a decent win at Shepparton. Herbertson will no doubt give him every chance to improve, so keep him safe. PICKLE IT (5) was disappointing last week, but that was a slightly harder race. He does run his best races when able to find the front, so he may be open to improvement. The chances don’t end there, with a case able to be made for most in the race, headed by MIKI MARK (4) and POWERLINC (3), who also go in the Early Quaddie. SELECTIONS:WAR ZONE (10), JUSTLIKEDAVE (7), TOMMYS LOOKOUT (6), PICKLE IT (5)

OVERVIEW: Incredibly challenging race and hard to be confident. BETTA THAN LOVE (3) has been well supported in his two runs since returning to Victoria. He had his chance two starts back when second, then tried to lead last time but was under pressure a lap out and was beaten by a space. The stewards’ report had enough detail to suggest there may have been excuses, and he could bounce back off that effort. Monitor betting for any added confidence. HOME AND DRY (9) hasn’t won since March, when he was able to lead, but you can make a case that this race looks to be his most suitable in some time. The form of this field suggests they are unlikely to be running fast times, which might be more comfortable for his sweet spot. He has a soft trailing draw to conserve and come with one run. CHASING THE WIND (4) worked mid-race here last week and was sound to the line in a slogging affair. He hasn’t won in well over a year, but Alford jumps on again, so he’s worth considering. DELTA STARZ (6) was a winner two starts back, although the form out of that race hasn’t necessarily stacked up. He has an in-form driver, which helps. I had ROCKROLL RAMBO (7) on top from the same draw last week and he was never a factor, working home fairly. He will likely be map-negative again, so has place claims, similar to REASON TO LAUGH (10), who will need the right tempo. SELECTIONS:BETTA THAN LOVE (3), HOME AND DRY (9), CHASING THE WIND (4), DELTA STARZ (6)

OVERVIEW:ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (3) is returning to more suitable grade after performing well in the VICBRED Series, where she ran home well without much luck in the final. There’s a form reference from Maryborough four starts back, where she was able to lead and was run down on the post by MONTANA PRIDE (4), who she meets here with a better draw. The stable is worth respecting as infrequent visitors to Cranbourne. MONTANA PRIDE (4) is racing very well, and his three runs at Melton since the race where they met have all been very good, with not much going his way on each occasion. He’s the testing material. KOSIMO (9) seems well suited with his claiming price dropping him significantly in class. Although he was poor last time, his runs haven’t been too bad at Melton and he was a winner there in May in much tougher grade. UBETTA KNOT (1) has been a little costly her past couple, but she has either had to work or had a tricky draw, and gets a much easier map this time. If they overcook things in front, she should get her chance along the sprint lane. PLATINUM JIVE (5) is a very nice mare who’s been freshened for this off a trial win at Bacchus Marsh. She has a very good record at this track and can sprint well off a helmet. She just has a sticky draw and will need the right tempo. SELECTIONS:ISTHISTHEREALLIFE (3), MONTANA PRIDE (4), KOSIMO (9), UBETTA KNOT (1)

OVERVIEW: MASTER LOUEY (5) was found on top from a soft pole draw here last week and ran well, just unable to sprint down the winner in a solid last half. This is a big drop in quality from what he faced last week and, now fitter fourth-up, he should be primed to put his best foot forward. You get the leading driver to navigate a sticky draw and give him every chance to be too strong for his rivals late in what looks a very suitable race. JUST PEDRO (8) looks to get the cosy run behind the likely leader here and conserve for one run late. He was a good winner last time at Ballarat and isn’t disadvantaged here being an ODM runner. OUR PINUP GIRL (6) was disappointing last week, but she was first-up and the market suggested she may need the outing. The stable goes well at this track and she’s worth another chance. BONA KHAN (1) will look to lead here, as he so often likes to do from these draws, and has been going okay. He just prefers the shorter distances, and seeing out this trip strongly is the concern. ILLAWONG PHOENIX (7) is going okay for the new stable but has a tricky draw to overcome and, although he will need luck, has solid claims at the minor end. BACK: MASTER LOUEY (5)– 4 units (win) SELECTIONS: MASTER LOUEY (5), JUST PEDRO (8), OUR PINUP GIRL (6), ILLAWONG PHOENIX (7)

OVERVIEW: LE GASTON (3) based on his SP profile alone, will start a short-priced favourite here, and on the strength of his first-up victory he deserves to head the market. He has overall been costly to punters, didn’t win by much at Kilmore, and the time wasn’t overly flash. He has a stable and driver in form and strikes a winnable race here. He’s not a “chips in” job at this stage, however. EAGLEYE (6) brings different form from NSW, where she was a last-start winner at Newcastle in decent time. More significantly, she joins a stable that has an excellent strike rate with horses new to the yard and often gets an upsurge in what they are able to produce. Watch the betting and include her in the Quaddie. MATRIARCH DAISY (5) is a 3yo filly who was in terrific form, but her last two runs have been well short of what she is capable of. She’s a go-forward type and her best form can win this, so keep her safe. STORM VENDETTA (4) was okay here last week in running second from a soft draw and is worth keeping safe again, as he should map okay. SELECTIONS: LE GASTON (3), EAGLEYE (6), MATRIARCH DAISY (5), STORM VENDETTA (4)

OVERVIEW:MAJESTIC CHARMA (8) finds a very suitable race with the mare’s allowance, being the sole runner off the back row and likely to map closer than she did last time out, when she rattled to the line in a slick closing section in a bigger and stronger field. She can tend to be a bit dicey at the start, but if she fills her action well, in this grade you can expect her to storm home late. JOU LOU (4) will no doubt be popular in the market on the back of winning four from six and developing a nice partnership with James Herbertson. He musters good gate speed and will look for the top end over the short trip, where he won last time. His times, however, haven’t been overly strong in weaker company, so although he ticks a lot of boxes, he does strike a better grade. BERTINELLI (7) is an interesting runner from NSW, where he hasn’t won in nearly a year but has been performing okay against largely Tuesday Menangle grade. He has a tricky draw to overcome but warrants respect. RIGHT OF REPLY (3) had every chance here and couldn’t sprint with them, but this does look a little more suitable and he should map well again. There are a number in the mix for the minor prize, including ATEGO DAWN (1), STEADY DREAM (2) and CARTALCHA (6). BACK: MAJESTIC CHARMA (8)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJESTIC CHARMA (8), JOU LOU (4), BERTINELLI (7), RIGHT OF REPLY (3)

OVERVIEW: UNCLE BILL (6) stands out here based on his maiden performance, where he showed good gate speed before taking cover and holding his ground against an above-average type who subsequently made the VICBRED Final. The exposed form of the others has been untrustworthy, so although you need to apply some caution with maiden trotters, this one is showing more positivity than the opposition. ALECTRONA (1) is getting closer to a win based on her past few performances and looks to map well here from the soft draw. Her times are comparable with the top pick and she can go close. ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8) has a solid SP profile but came through the same race as the top pick last time out and galloped in running, although he was dropping out prior. He’s a great looker and can improve if the penny drops. CASUAL CONNECTION (4) is a NSW visitor from a strong stable who’s only had the one run, where she broke three times in running. She’s had plenty of trials, but the penny is yet to drop. She goes in merely out of respect for the stable, as she’s yet to command confidence based on performance. BACK: UNCLE BILL (6)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:UNCLE BILL (6), ALECTRONA (1), ALDEBARAN MIGUEL (8), CASUAL CONNECTION (4)

OVERVIEW: JILLIBY STRANGER (4) is a 2yo taking on older horses here, but he did so last time out when able to win his maiden at Terang after getting a perfect trip behind the leader. I’m not sure how strong that form is, but he will be better for the outing. It’s also unclear exactly how he maps here, but he will no doubt be popular in the market given the respect the stable commands in a race of this nature. CARUSO STAR (6) looks well suited as an 11-time winner, whereas many of the opposition have only won their maiden. He’s fitter now fourth-up and, more importantly, goes to the front row and has a draw to use his gate speed. He beat a better field two starts back here when mapping softly. QUICK CRUNCH (5) is a fast beginner and has been racing consistently overall this season. She was a winner five starts back when able to lead and control before just scraping home. Since then, she either hasn’t had the right draws or set-ups but has still been sound. She’s a winner at this track and, if she finds the top, will take running down. OPERTSER (1) was a winner two starts back, beating CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (7), with both driven to run on and performing well. They’ve both placed again since and must be given claims in a race with different form lines to assess. SELECTIONS:JILLIBY STRANGER (4), CARUSO STAR (6), QUICK CRUNCH (5), OPERTSER (1)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG MARICRUZ (4) is a horse you will be able to get a strong line on, as she ran second to the top pick in the previous race last time at Terang, where she led and had every chance but was okay. If JILLIBY STRANGER happens to do the job in the previous race, her stocks will rise. Aside from that, the time she ran there may be good enough to get the job done this time, and with a smart stable behind her and tactical speed, she’s the starting point. RIDE HIGH CAPTAIN (2) is open to sharp improvement in his numerical form after a sound fifth here last week in a stronger race, and prior to that stuck on okay for second when sitting parked. He may map to get the right run and get his chance late. KING BALDWIN (6) has only had the one trial for the new stable, which was sound, and now makes his debut after plenty of experience at the trials in NSW. He’s hard to get a line on, but the trainer/driver combination warrants respect. MEGALODON (1) is another first starter who’s been at the Bacchus Marsh trials, which are inconclusive, but he is a market watch from the soft draw. SELECTIONS:KEAYANG MARICRUZ (4), RIDE HIGH CAPTAIN (2), KING BALDWIN (6), MEGALODON (1)

WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2) has been a consistent performer and should be suited by the mile distance here. His chances would be enhanced significantly if SHEMEANSBUSINESS (1) decides to take a sit this week after disappointing when leading over the same distance last start, albeit in quick time. MERRYWOOD PAUL (6) gets into this race well with the claim and could be the improver if there is some genuine tempo throughout. The three Wayne Yole-trained runners, NATIONAL NEWS (3), CAN FEEL THE FURY (4) and JAMES CAGNEY (5), are likely to be saved for one run and will also be relying on some solid tempo throughout to allow them to finish over the top of the favoured runners. Selections:WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), SHEMEANSBUSINESS (1), MERRYWOOD PAUL (6), NATIONAL NEWS (3) Staking Strategy: Will be reliant on some good speed throughout, but MERRYWOOD PAUL could be running over the top for the in-form driver Ethan Arnott with his claim. 1 unit each-way – MERRYWOOD PAUL (6).

A competitive No More Than Four Wins event, where Victorian visitor VIVID DREAM (7) brings some handy form to the state. She has undergone a stable change since her last start and may have to settle towards the rear of the field, but she looks the class horse of the race and may simply be too quick for them up the home straight with a nice run in transit. I GOTTA GO (3) broke through for a deserved victory last start after being unlucky on numerous occasions prior and should have enough gate speed to be first to the pegs here. There doesn't appear to be a lot of mid-race pressure unless ITZBUDDHA (4) grabs hold and pulls, so he should get every chance to finish on the podium. ROCKY STRIDE (5) drops back in grade after performing well in feature races of late and made good ground in a sharp mile last start. He possesses a very quick finishing burst when asked and looks a strong chance here. OUR WILLOW (6) is a four-year-old mare who clearly has plenty of ability when right. Her form has tapered off of late, but a change of scenery to a new stable may be the spark she needs to recapture her best. TAPPY (2) broke through for her first victory in the state last start, producing some nice closing sectionals to score. He should secure a nice run on speed with cover and gets every chance to finish on the podium again. Selections:VIVID DREAM (7), I GOTTA GO (3), ROCKY STRIDE (5), TAPPY (2) Staking Strategy: Hard not to respect winning Victorian form, so expect VIVID DREAM to be hard to beat. We’ll play the quinella with I GOTTA GO who should be first to the pegs. 2 unit quinella – I GOTTA GO (3) and VIVID DREAM (7).

IDEN OLIVER (2) has been quite dominant in his past two victories, recording good time over the middle distance, and again draws to get a nice run on speed here, gaining entry with the claim for driver Grace Jones. He may cop some early pressure from the Geoff Smith-prepared pair LIKEABLE ROGUE (3) and IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (6), but he should still get his chance to find a position on speed and be right in the finish. Both of those stablemates have been racing consistently of late and are due to break through for another victory, with their chances enhanced if either can find the pegs. KENYA (8) draws an awkward inside back-row gate but should appreciate some genuine tempo throughout and will be dangerous if the gaps come his way. JET TO HEAVEN (1) has broken at both starts since arriving in the state but could be right in the finish if he brings his best manners from the pole draw. TULLAH GIRL (4) uses the double claim to gain entry into this race and, if able to find a nice run in transit, should be running home strongly. Selections:IDEN OLIVER (2), LIKEABLE ROGUE (3), IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (6), KENYA (8) Staking Strategy: Hard to knock winning form, so IDEN OLIVER should take beating again here from the nice draw. 2 unit win – IDEN OLIVER (2).

The only full field of the night is for the maidens over the mile, where the talented but erratic SHIBASAKI (11) resumes from a break. He trialled nicely a month ago and has since undergone a stable change, and if he brings his best behaviour, he could take some holding out late. IDEN MISS WORLD (4) could be the improver, as I have her finding the pegs with her good gate speed. She also trialled nicely in handy time two weeks ago, and that form would see her right in the finish here. LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (9) is always thereabouts in races of this nature and should get a nice run through from the back-row draw to be running home strongly again. ARRIVAL TIME (8) draws an awkward gate but produced a handy enough performance first up in the state after doing some work, and should be in the finish if the gaps come his way. Selections:SHIBASAKI (11), IDEN MISS WORLD (4), LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (9), ARRIVAL TIME (8) Staking Strategy:SHIBASAKI could demolish them here if he brought his best behaviour, but siding with a small play on IDEN MISS WORLD at odds, as can run a cheeky race in front over the short distance. 0.5 unit win, 1.5 unit place – IDEN MISS WORLD (4).

WEONA EAGLE (1) has returned to form over her past two starts and gets the handy draw to have options from the gate here. Expect INTO THE HARKNESS (2) and MUZZAME MATE (3) to push forward from their draws, while MY WAY (5) and LETSGOBRO (7) may also press forward with their good gate speed. That could set the race up nicely for the back-row runners WE SALUTE YOU (9) and MOVESLIKEALADY (10) to be finishing over the top. Both have been racing in good form of late and just need a nice run in transit to be strong winning chances here. JOHN VINCENT (6) would be expected to be driven with a sit and is another who could be finishing home strongly if he can get a nice cart into the race. Selections:WE SALUTE YOU (9), MOVESLIKEALADY (10), WEONA EAGLE (1), MUZZAME MATE (3) Staking Strategy: Looks to be speed galore on here, so happy to play a couple of back-row horses. 1 unit win – WE SALUTE YOU (9) and MOVESLIKEALADY (10).

There looks to be a stack of speed here over the short-course distance, led by LYNRYD SKYNRYD (4) and WAVES OF CHANCE (6) from the middle front-row draws. WAVES OF CHANCE (6) clearly has plenty of ability and, if he can find the pegs and settle in running, could take plenty of running down. ANOTHER NIEN (8) should be a beneficiary of the hot speed throughout and, as the lone back-row runner following the scratching of the expected favourite, should be able to work into the running line and finish home strongly late. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2) broke a long run of outs to score last start, hitting the line well, and looks set to receive another nice run on speed with cover here, giving him every chance to record back-to-back victories. Selections:ANOTHER NIEN (8), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2), WAVES OF CHANCE (6), CENTURIAN MISS (1) Staking Strategy: Expecting them to go silly here over the short distance, which should mean ANOTHER NIEN gets his chance to finish over the top. 1 unit win – ANOTHER NIEN (8).

The Free For All is an intriguing race, with the speed map likely to depend on whether PARDOE PLUGGA (5) and WATERMELON SUGAR (6) use their brilliant gate speed to attempt to find the pegs first. BETTABLACK TIGER (2) was good first up for the new stable and expect he may be driven more conservatively here from the nice draw after being from the pole last start. He should take plenty of beating with clear running. CUSTOM HARLEY (4) would be expected to be put into the race at some stage and is always thereabouts in the finish in races of this nature, while GO THE RED (8) will be relying on some solid tempo up front to allow him to finish home strongly, as he has done numerous times of late since arriving in the state. Selections:BETTABLACK TIGER (2), CUSTOM HARLEY (4), GO THE RED (8), WATERMELON SUGAR (6) Staking Strategy: Thinking BETTABLACK TIGER will prove too classy here, no matter where he sits, and break through for the new stable. 3 unit win – BETTABLACK TIGER (2).

The low-class race rounds out the night, where there looks to be a bit of speed engaged from the front row. KYRGIOS (1) makes his first start for the Brent Parish stable and looks to have sufficient gate speed to hold a forward position. His mainland form prior to arriving in Tasmania has to be respected in a race of this nature. DANCINWIVJOLENE (2) is also first up from a break and gets a nice draw to kick-start her campaign, having been super competitive in races of this grade previously. MIDNITE DESIRE (4) was well fancied in the market at both starts after arriving interstate but was only fair despite receiving nice runs in transit. He has since had a let-up, so an improved effort wouldn't surprise, although the market may be the best guide. OUR SWEET TRIXIE (5) is always earning cheques but strikes an awkward draw, as does CHRIS BE QUICK (9), who loves filling a placing in races of this nature. MODERN JIVE (8) resumes from a let-up and could be the one at odds if he can secure a soft run along the pegs and the gaps appear late. Selections:KYRGIOS (1), DANCINWIVJOLENE (2), MIDNITE DESIRE (4), MODERN JIVE (8) Staking Strategy:MODERN JIVE first up, looks to get a soft peg run over his preferred distance and is worthy of a dabble at each-way odds. 1 unit each-way – MODERN JIVE (8). OVERVIEW:MICHEN ROY (4) returns to the front row after three challenging draws off the back, one of which he was able to overcome to win at this track two starts back, albeit in easier company. He copped a check last start at Melton when getting to the line fairly in a much tougher race. He will appreciate the middle trip and the opportunity to roll forward and use his strength. MOMENTUM SHIFT (3) can be a sharp improver on his numerical form, drawn well for the first time in a while and able to map positively. He’s been okay in much tougher grade than this and should represent good value. HELLOVATIME (5) is a very honest type who’s only finished outside the top four once in sixteen starts this season. He was a winner in good time two starts back at Wagga and was up in grade last start, where he missed narrowly after getting a good run. He’s a strong chance of getting the job done again if he gets the right trip. LILLY LOTUS (6) hasn’t been at her best this season, but she has been racing against strong company throughout. She was in the stewards’ report after her last start at Melton and, based on that, we can expect a more conservative drive, but her best is good enough. CEE CEE LOU (8) is worth including in the Early Quaddie. He’s second-up and was okay in a sprint home last time. He has a cosy draw and does enjoy this circuit. SELECTIONS:MICHEN ROY (4), MOMENTUM SHIFT (3), HELLOVATIME (5), LILLY LOTUS (6)

OVERVIEW:SOHO PLAYGIRL (9) joins the in-form Turnbull stable after the sad passing of Ted Jepsen in July, and victory would be fitting for his memory. She’s had one trial and ran well there, and although she’s normally better suited off the front row, she does follow out some speedy ones. Last preparation she was racing in tougher grade than this and will give this a real shake fresh-up. MADAM REACTOR (6) will run the gate, and her regular pattern is to take cover thereafter. She’s been racing honestly and likes this track, so will get her chance if that pattern eventuates. HES CHARLIES ANGEL (2) has the chance to improve on his numerical form, dropping back to a suitable grade. He has gate speed and will look for the top end, which could assist him in breaking a long run of outs. IM DUSTEE (7) is first-up from a bad draw here and will need plenty of luck, but he loves this track and his best form is better than most here. AMERICAN MICHI (10) has been in the tips plenty of times and he does have ability, but he’s starting to become a little frustrating with his manners. Keep him safe. The chances don’t end there, with CORNISHTOWN KID (1) and AXIS ANGEL (8) having minor claims for exotics from soft draws. SELECTIONS:SOHO PLAYGIRL (9), MADAM REACTOR (6), HES CHARLIES ANGEL (2), IM DUSTEE (7)

OVERVIEW:ALTO CORRAGIO (9) is giving away experience here as a 2yo having only his second start, but his performance on debut was solid after looking good at the trials. He looks likely to get a good run through and map well over the short trip, and with added fitness and the in-form stable, he looks a winning chance against even opposition. PIASTRI (4) is a 3yo who was good first-up, running into a smart 2yo and having to overcome a tricky draw on that occasion. That was the best run of his career so far, so a repeat has him right in it. MAJOR FRIEND (8) is a 3yo filly who’s been a model of consistency, placing six times from seven starts this season. She gets a soft draw and will need luck at some stage, but is in the mix. Outside of those, it will come down to who gets the best run for the third and fourth spots, with DEXTERS DONE (2), CAPTAIN MILO (3) and DONTTELLNANNA (10) heading those chances. BACK: ALTO CORRAGIO (9) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:ALTO CORRAGIO (9), PIASTRI (4), MAJOR FRIEND (8), DONTTELLNANNA (10)

OVERVIEW: MAJESTIC MONARCH (4) won as an odds-on favourite when able to lead two starts back, then failed last time out, but it was a luckless run where he settled back in the field and was coming hard late, only to be denied clear running at a vital stage. In this company and from this draw, expect a more assertive drive at the start and for him to be hard to run down. DOSSIER (2) has been creeping down in grade each start and sucking me in, and she looks well placed again based on what her best level is capable of. She’s not a brilliant beginner, but if she can map behind the speed, or at worst three pegs, she’s a strong chance on a value basis. DISTANT SUN (10) will find this company more suitable than recent starts, and the claim of Blake Pace helps his chances. That pair combined for victory five starts back at Kilmore and can be strong late. CENTURION DREAM (11) will deservedly have some market support and does strike easier opposition, but she won’t have the opportunity to use her speed and map well, which is a slight negative. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (3) can normally show speed but mixes her tactics as to whether she holds the front or takes cover. She’s been fair lately, although there have been higher expectations based on her SP profile. BACK: MAJESTIC MONARCH (4)– 1.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:MAJESTIC MONARCH (4), DOSSIER (2), DISTANT SUN (10), CENTURION DREAM (11)

OVERVIEW: FINAL BOW (9) ticks a lot of boxes here in the right grade, dropping significantly in class and racing at her favourite track, where she’s only missed a place six times from eighteen starts. She draws out behind a couple of speedy beginners, which should allow her to map into a striking position, with the top driver at this track aboard to time things to perfection. She’s won her past three starts here, producing strong closing sectionals each time, and looks primed to do so again. SMOKING SHANNON (10) looks the testing material, having put in three solid performances for the new stable, including a win three starts back at this track. She goes to the back row, which is a disadvantage, but she’s still a solid chance. MYNAMEISRUBY (3) will show her usual early speed and give plenty of cheek over her favourite distance. Her times are limited compared to what the top pick can produce, however. TOPHUT JOHNY (8) will benefit from a cosy run and can come with one burst over the concluding stages. Navigating traffic limits his winning chances, but he has place claims. In fact, there are a few in the hunt for minor exotics in ATOMIC GLORY (2), WHERES WOOD WOOD (5) and FAVOURITEHIGHLIGHT (7) with the right runs. BACK: FINAL BOW (9)– 3.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: FINAL BOW (9), SMOKING SHANNON (10), MYNAMEISRUBY (3), TOPHUT JOHNY (8)

OVERVIEW: A race mixing 2yos, 3yos and older horses. CORBIE LAIDIR (2) is a 2yo making his debut for the Pitt stable, which continues to produce quality youngsters this season. In a recent trial here, he ran second to a smart one, which measures up very well for this. He can press forward from this favourable draw, and any market push would only add to the confidence levels. TOUCH OF REALITY (6) is a model of consistency without winning, and she went within a whisker of winning at Maryborough last start when able to lead. She’s in the mix again, albeit from a sticky draw. MUDDY (5) has been freshened with a trial since his debut second at this track, where he was able to map well from a tricky draw and performed well. He has decent ability and is worth respecting on what he’s shown. Then we have the two first-starting 3yos, COASTAL ELEGANCE (3) and ULTIMATE GRANGE (7), who have trialled okay but would need a significant market push to consider as winning chances. BACK: CORBIE LAIDIR (2)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: CORBIE LAIDIR (2), TOUCH OF REALITY (6), MUDDY (5), ULTIMATE GRANGE (7)

OVERVIEW:HEZ HARRYWHO(8) is awkwardly drawn but well graded and gets Herbertson, which is a factor in a very even race. The pair combined for victory when together three starts back at this track in decent time, when mapping on the peg line. He will need the breaks at the right time but has upside. MAMMALS REASON (6) is in terrific form, racing tough in similar company to this. She’s won three of her last five, so even though this map is tricky, she warrants respect. ALTA BAYAMO (5) was a very good winner here two starts back when able to lead, then was very disappointing last time when appearing to have every chance. He does return to the front row, so perhaps that’s a positive. ELLEEGANT LANE (3) had been racing consistently before turning in a terrific performance to win at Melton by a space, albeit against easier opposition. It’s not an easy race and is a wide Quaddie leg, as you can make a case for a few, including HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), TOTALLY STUNNING and HELLOVASTORY. SELECTIONS: HEZ HARRYWHO(8), MAMMALS REASON (6), ALTA BAYAMO (5), ELLEEGANT LANE (3)

OVERVIEW:FEEL THE REIGN (8) seems well placed as the winningest horse in this race, and his last couple of runs have been encouraging. These concession-driver races often rotate the same horses, so he looks to bring different form. He races well when he can come with one burst, so if he gets the breaks, he can flash late. OUR MYSTERY BET (6) continues to race well and is also performing better on the clock sectionally; he just doesn’t seem to crack it for a win. This race does appear suitable and, with the right run, he will be tough in the finish. THE IRISHMAN (1) was a good winner here four starts back when sitting parked and was too strong for his rivals, albeit in easier grade. He should get a good map and give plenty of cheek. REGAL ROCK (5) can show speed from this draw and is a winner at this track when finding the top. He hasn’t saluted since February, but if he gets the right passage he could improve. SELECTIONS:FEEL THE REIGN (8), OUR MYSTERY BET (6), THE IRISHMAN (1), REGAL ROCK (5)

OVERVIEW:NEDS BEACH (2) has been racing fairly in SA lately and gets a favourable draw to map well, with Herbertson jumping aboard. His win five starts back would be good enough to measure up here in what looks a tricky and even bunch of horses. BETTERTHANABOUGHTONE (3) was able to win at this track back in January and beat some of these on that occasion. She has a consistent SP profile and her map gives her a solid winning chance. MISS HERMES (6) can be a little hard to catch, being a winner in an easier race at Leeton two starts back but not quite living up to market expectations around that. Her best performance gives her a strong winning hope. KNOW THE SCORE (5) is a quick beginner and led all the way to win four starts back, which was his best performance this season. A positive map increases his chances. SELECTIONS:NEDS BEACH (2), BETTERTHANABOUGHTONE (3), MISS HERMES (6), KNOW THE SCORE (5)

OVERVIEW: QUEENS BOULEVARD (4) trailed the leader, moved into the one out and one back trail at the 500m and tried hard when second behind Sweetsugarcandyman in a handy mile rate of 1.56.9 at Ballarat. She has shown promise at her two starts to date and gets her chance to break through for a win. VINCENT ORILEY (1) led out then took cover when second behind Sporty Rocks at Ararat last outing. He is drawn to receive every chance again and is worth a ticket each way. WICKED TORQUE (2) was also placed after trailing the leader throughout at her latest attempt and is a place chance again. MISS ADELIA (3) is a first starter for trainer Donna Bourke, which was runner up at a recent Mount Gambier trial effort and must be kept safe. ANGELIC (5) is also a newcomer to Victoria after being safely held in two Tasmanian starts. She is widely drawn but is a possible improver. SELECTIONS: QUEENS BOULEVARD (4), VINCENT ORILEY (1), WICKED TORQUE (2), MISS ADELIA (3)

OVERVIEW:BETTING ATTACK (4) broke through for his maiden success after leading out then taking cover at Maryborough. He is likely to utilize his gate speed to find a prominent position again and this race isn’t too much harder so he should give a bold showing. EASTBRO MIKA (1) was held up for a run at a vital stage and didn’t have much luck when third at Terang two starts ago then endured a tough trip on the outside of the leader throughout when a creditable fifth at Maryborough. She must be considered as a winning chance from the pole position. MILOLA ROCK (7) got a long way back and couldn’t work into the race in a slick final half of 56.7 seconds at Maryborough last week. Her form prior was sound and she possesses a powerful finishing burst so she is worth an investment. MARGARITARI (6) continues to race consistently having only missed a top four position once at her past twelve attempts. She is a versatile pacer and must be included amongst the leading chances. SELECTIONS: BETTING ATTACK (4), EASTBRO MIKA (1), MILOLA ROCK (7), MARGARITARI (6)

OVERVIEW: HURRICANE HOOLY (4) performed below expectations when ninth at Melton last outing but the mile rate was a slick 1.55.4 and her form prior was sound. She defeated Final Bow (won twice since) at Bendigo in a mile rate of 1.57.8 in July. ZWICK (5) led throughout to win at Terang then found the line well from the second half of the field (not as fast as the winner) when fourth at Melton on Wednesday. This race is no harder and he should be competitive again. KIMCHI (1) attempted to lead throughout and peaked late when sixth at Maryborough last week. He disappointed last time but he is usually competitive against this class and he is ideally drawn so he is worth another chance. WINGATE GUY (6) worked forward to find the lead at the 1700m and was run down at the end when fifth at Swan Hill. He trailed the leader throughout when a close second at Shepparton prior and he should be competitive under these conditions. SELECTIONS: HURRICANE HOOLY (4), ZWICK (5), KIMCHI (1), WINGATE GUY (6)

OVERVIEW: FARROH JOE (2) is a smart 2yo pacer and should appreciate a drop back in class on his past two efforts in the Super Series. He ran home well for second behind Smack Bang Bart in a heat then he had to use plenty of energy in the early stages to find the position behind the leader when seventh in a semi-final. PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1) led throughout to score at Ararat two starts ago then had little luck from a wide draw at Terang. He appears to be better placed under these conditions and should be competitive again. JUST LIKE NUGGET (3) finished off best to defeat Blue Miki (won since) at a Ballarat victory after a close up third behind PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1). This is a race of similar standard and he should be competitive again. TORQUE INTHEUSA (4) will appreciate a significant drop back in class for this assignment and was placed behind the in-form pacer Gold In Paris three starts ago so she is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: FARROH JOE (2), PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (1), JUST LIKE NUGGET (3), TORQUE INTHEUSA (4)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR LINCOLN (6) has performed extremely well in two starts since returning from Queensland. He gave the winner Keayang Crippa a big start and made many lengths in the final quarter when an eye-catching second at Mildura last outing. He should prove hard to beat against this line up. FREAK OUT (8) raced without cover throughout when second behind Lenard Ess at Melton two starts ago then worked too hard in a slick mile of 1.55.4 at Cranbourne last time out. He gets into this race nicely with a concession claim and should run a good race. MISSMALACHITE (7) is a tough mare, which led throughout to win at Ararat two starts ago then drew on the second line at her latest unplaced performance. She is racing well enough to figure in the finish. ESPERANZA (4) was safely held at Swan Hill last week but was a winner at Kilmore prior and cannot be left out of calculations. SELECTIONS: MAJOR LINCOLN (6), FREAK OUT (8), MISSMALACHITE (7), ESPERANZA (4)

OVERVIEW:POPPY POPSTAR (7) won over Boutika (won since in track record time) on August 03 and has won five races for the season. She has been a little below her best form at her past three attempts but she strikes a suitable assignment now so she should go well. SONARMI JOH (9) is a fast beginner from the standing start and is racing consistently. He was runner up behind Boutika in record time at Ararat two starts ago then wasn’t beaten by far at his latest Terang fifth. WHOSHOTTHEPIEMAN (8) was poorly away and lost all chance at his only standing start attempt but he was very impressive at his latest Swan Hill victory, where he led throughout. He won well enough last time to suggest he will prove hard to beat if he is able to get away safely. ITGETSBETTER (4) was runner up after trailing the leader under similar conditions at Terang two starts ago then it appeared as though he would run second again but he broke stride with 100m remaining at his latest fifth. His main rivals are all commencing from bigger handicaps so he must be respected. SELECTIONS: POPPY POPSTAR (7), SONARMI JOH (9), WHOSHOTTHEPIEMAN (8), ITGETSBETTER (4)

OVERVIEW: TORQUE IN HEAVEN (8) settled midfield, came out three horses wide from the 700m and sustained a long run to win at Maryborough last week. This race is no harder and he should prove hard to beat again if he has normal luck from the awkward draw. IAMAWINGATE (5) was safely held at Swan Hill last outing but this is a drop back in class and he was beaten by a narrow margin at Ararat three starts ago. He possesses brilliant gate speed and he usually performs best when he is able to lead out then take cover. SKADI (4) began quickly and was able to lead throughout at Swan Hill when resuming since April. This is a race of more depth but she should have benefited from her first up performance and is drawn to go well again. COOPER CHUBB (2) has been placed in a trial since finishing last of nine in a heat of the Super Series and NORMANDY NUGGET (3) possesses the early speed to gain a prominent position in the early stages. SELECTIONS: TORQUE IN HEAVEN (8), IAMAWINGATE (5), SKADI (4), NORMANDY NUGGET (3)

OVERVIEW: GOLD IN PARIS (5) is racing in career best form having won at her past three attempts and should prove hard to beat again. She was without cover early, pressured the leader and found the front at the 1800m when she held off a strong field to win at Terang last outing. KING KASEY (4) looms as the obvious threat. He held the lead from the pole position and dashed home in a slick final quarter of 27.7 seconds when he won at Swan Hill last week. OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (2) is better than her form reads and should run a good race under these conditions. She led out, took cover at the 1400m and had no clear run at the finish when an unlucky sixth at Ballarat last outing. ROCKELLA (6) recorded a handy mile rate of 1.55.3 after racing without cover at Ballarat then competed at Metropolitan level at his latest fifth. He is widely drawn but is not without a chance. SELECTIONS: GOLD IN PARIS (5), KING KASEY (4), OUR ULTIMATE GRACY (2), ROCKELLA (6)

HUNGRY FOR MORE (1) took on a much stronger race last time out taken out by Northview Cruncha in good time at Albion Park. This filly was good running into fourth there and is likely to have derived a lot of benefit from the outing. TUSCANS COURAGE (4) was forced to race without cover last time out when finishing second behind Swedesboro. He could secure a similar run and should be thereabouts again. LIGHTYEAR (3) took on a much stronger race last time out when finishing fourth behind Medellin at Redcliffe. He should settle close in the run and can be running on late. WHATA SWEETY (6) didn’t run well on debut when giving ground and being beaten a big margin in sixth. The trial prior to his return was better and he may run a better race second up. SELECTIONS: HUNGRY FOR MORE (1), TUSCANS COURAGE (4), LIGHTYEAR (3), WHATA SWEETY (6) SUGGESTED BET: HUNGRY FOR MORE (1) to win.

OLIVIA RHAYNE BOW (7) secured a good run on the pegs last time out and wasn’t beaten too far in fourth behind Dancinwith pleasure. She is likely to find this a lot easier and can be put into the race at some stage. KIPCHOGE (3) led last time out and was well beaten by Imasillybilly but did go well enough in third to suggest he should be hard to beat in a race of this nature. He may be able to press forward and if he found the lead he would likely be hard to beat. TEN AND TWO (6) secured a good run last time out and wasn’t beaten far there in second behind Hez Our Playboy at this track. He should secure a good run again and can be thereabouts. AZZIF (1) had an issue in her latest start which saw her well beaten there. Her trials weren’t good enough to suggest she could win a race but she has since landed back in the stable of Graham Dwyer and is worth keeping in mind from the good draw. SELECTIONS: OLIVIA RHAYNE BOW (7), KIPCHOGE (3), TEN AND TWO (6), AZZIF (1) SUGGESTED BET: OLIVIA RHAYNE BOW (7) to win.

JILLIBY PANDA (2) has good gate speed and should find himself on the front in this race. He was seemingly quite disappointing last time out when securing a good run on the pegs and fading out of it late. He can look to bounce back. EBONY BELLE (7) took on a stronger race last time out taken out by Sammys Secret at Redcliffe. She draws nicely in this race and can be running on late. SUBTLE CHAY (4) ran fairly last time out in a heat of the showcase series when sitting leaders back and fading out of it late. He was first up there and is likely to have derived benefit from the run. STONES (3) has good gate speed but does draw outside of a horse with equally good gate speed which could make it hard for him to get across early. He is capable with the right run. SELECTIONS: JILLIBY PANDA (2), EBONY BELLE (7), SUBTLE CHAY (4), STONES (3) SUGGESTED BET: JILLIBY PANDA (2) to win.

THE BLACK FOX (1) often doesn’t show a lot of gate speed which could make this draw a touch tricky. He was very good last time out when running on into second behind Britts Mate which looks good form for a race of this nature. MY ULTIMATE LOUIE (6) should get a good run through behind a horse which will be keen to hold a forward position in this race. He ran a reasonable third placing behind Bokhari two back before taking on a heat of the showcase series at Redcliffe. ROSEANNE RUBY (10) did a lot of work last time out which she isn’t suited to and was well beaten in fourth behind Britts Mate. She finds a very suitable race but does draw outside the back row this time. SHADYS DELIGHT (4) hasn’t started for over a month which does appear to be a significant query coming into this race. He ran well for third last time out behind Downtown Manhattan having been forced to do the work outside the leader. SELECTIONS: THE BLACK FOX (1), MY ULTIMATE LOUIE (6), ROSEANNE RUBY (10), SHADYS DELIGHT (4) SUGGESTED BET: THE BLACK FOX (1) to win.

TEACHERS PET (1) hasn’t been racing at her best but has always been a horse which runs her best races out in front and should get that opportunity in this race. She wasn’t suited last start when sitting outside the leader in a race taken out by Vodka En Ice. AZOR AHAI (3) ran sixth last time out at Albion Park but wasn’t beaten far there by Galvarino. He should settle close enough in the run and appears to find a suitable type of race. SKYLAR BREE (6) looked particularly unlucky last time out at Redcliffe when being shuffled right back before running on strongly late into fifth. She comes into this race fourth up from a spell and lands an ideal draw. HOLME BOY (7) ran on strongly into second two starts ago before Wicked Mack at this track. He should get a similar run and can be fnishing it off late again. SELECTIONS: TEACHERS PET (1), AZOR AHAI (3), SKYLAR BREE (6), HOLME BOY (7) SUGGESTED BET: TEACHERS PET (1) to win.

ONE LAST ROLL (4) raced without cover at this track recently and was a good close up second behind Absolutely Stoked. Despite getting on in age he continues to race well and loves to race at this track. GIDUP CAPTAIN (1) has good gate speed and should be able to drive through and lead in this race. He hasn’t led for some time but does love racing on the pegs and has performed well leading previously. PRINCE OF PAIN (5) appears to be a real standout on class in this race but does appear to map quite awkwardly in this race with a few runners drawn underneath likely to be keen to hold forward positions. LULU LUCIFER (8) should get a good run off the speed and will be needing the race run to suit to bring her into it. Her latest win came when able to lead all the way at this track. SELECTIONS: ONE LAST ROLL (4), GIDUP CAPTAIN (1), PRINCE OF PAIN (5), LULU LUCIFER (8) SUGGESTED BET: ONE LAST ROLL (4) to win.

PUMPKIN PAT (4) has the slight barrier draw advantage on what looks to be her main danger in this race. She was able to burn through off the back row last time out to find the lead and was just run down late by Saturday Dance. BUDDY PERFECT (5) led and won two starts ago at Redcliffe beating Great Achiever. He looks likely to be forced to work in this race which could make things tough. STORMTIDE (6) looked to be a touch unlucky last time out at Redcliffe when being held up at a crucial stage before flashing into second. He should get a similar run and will just be relying on some luck at a crucial stage. ROCKIN SWEET (1) was able to score his latest win when leading and holding off Mach Assassin at this track. He may look to lead again in this race and should be thereabouts. SELECTIONS: PUMPKIN PAT (4), BUDDY PERFECT (5), STORMTIDE (6), ROCKIN SWEET (1) SUGGESTED BET: PUMPKIN PAT (4) to win.

DENIS THE PUNTER (2) may be able to press forward and find the lead in the early stages of this race. He is first up since July which does look a query. If he is ready to go first up he should run well. FLY BURRA (7) looked to be quite unlucky last start when crossed in the early stages before being held up at a crucial stage behind Absolutely Stoked. He should get a good run behind the speed in this race and can be running on late. STUDLEIGH ANNE (5) was well beaten last time out behind Ideal Pursuit in a race which didn’t pan out favourably for her. This race looks a bit easier than her latest outing and she can look to bounce back. BRITTS MATE (8) was able to sweep home over the top late to score last time out at Redcliffe. She rated reasonable time and can look to back that up in this race. SELECTIONS: DENIS THE PUNTER (2), FLY BURRA (7), STUDLEIGH ANNE (5), BRITTS MATE (8) SUGGESTED BET: FLY BURRA (7) to win.
